---
title: "Dashboards with Livewire"
---

Build Livewire components whose phiz charts follow the component's state. The page has two separate examples:

- **A minimal component** charts revenue from an application's own `orders` table, with one filter.
- **A linked dashboard** charts the bundled `mpg` car data, so it runs as written, with three charts that share filters.

**Requirements:** a Laravel application with Livewire 3, and `composer require phpstats/phiz phpstats/phibble phpstats/phplyr`.

## A minimal component

One chart of monthly revenue per customer from an `orders` table, filtered by sales channel.

`app/Livewire/RevenueByMonth.php`:

```php
namespace App\Livewire;

use App\Models\Order;
use Livewire\Component;
use Phibble\DataFrame;
use Phiz\Plot;

use function Phplyr\{
    col, floor_date, group_by, mutate, sum, summarize,
};

class RevenueByMonth extends Component
{
    public string $channel = 'All';

    public function render()
    {
        $orders = Order::query()->when(
            $this->channel !== 'All',
            fn ($q) => $q->where('channel', $this->channel),
        );

        $monthly = DataFrame::fromQuery($orders) |>
            mutate(
                month: floor_date(col('placed_on'), 'month'),
            ) |>
            group_by('month', 'customer') |>
            summarize(revenue: sum('total'));

        $chart = Plot::of($monthly)
            ->aes(x: 'month', y: 'revenue', color: 'customer')
            ->line()
            ->point()
            ->labs(x: null, y: 'Revenue ($)', color: null)
            ->size('container', 260);

        return view('livewire.revenue-by-month', [
            'chart' => $chart,
        ]);
    }
}
```

`resources/views/livewire/revenue-by-month.blade.php`:

```blade
<div>
    <select wire:model.live="channel">
        <option>All</option>
        <option>Web</option>
        <option>App</option>
        <option>Marketplace</option>
    </select>

    <x-phiz :plot="$chart" />
</div>
```

- **Redrawing.** Livewire reruns `render()` after each property change. `<x-phiz>` redraws the chart when its specification changes.
- **Server-side data.** The query, the monthly summary, and the chart are built in PHP. The page receives only the summarized rows.
- **Width.** `size('container', 260)` makes the chart fill its element's width at a fixed height.

## A linked dashboard

Three charts follow the same filters: a drive and a year selected in the page, and a vehicle class selected from a list. A shared function builds the charts, a component holds the state, and a view lays them out.

### The shared function

`fuel_dashboard()` takes the cars table and the filter state. It returns three plots and the class summary behind the bar chart. The file is [`examples/dashboard.php`](https://github.com/phpstats/phiz/blob/main/examples/dashboard.php), and [`examples/dashboard.chain.php`](https://github.com/phpstats/phiz/blob/main/examples/dashboard.chain.php) is the method-chain version.

{{< include _generated/source-dashboard.md >}}

- **Selection.** A computed `selected` field colors the selected class in the bar chart.
- **One fit.** The scatterplot's linear fit sets `inheritAes: false`, so it fits all filtered cars together instead of one line per class.
- **Trend.** The trend chart ignores the year filter, so both years stay visible.

With front-wheel drive, 2008, and the compact class selected, the charts look like this:

{{< include _generated/dashboard-preview.md >}}

### The component

`app/Livewire/FuelDashboard.php`:

```php
namespace App\Livewire;

use Livewire\Attributes\Url;
use Livewire\Component;
use Phibble\DataFrame;
use Phiz\Datasets;

class FuelDashboard extends Component
{
    #[Url]
    public ?string $drive = null;

    #[Url]
    public ?int $year = null;

    public ?string $selected = null;

    public function select(string $class): void
    {
        $this->selected = $this->selected === $class
            ? null
            : $class;
    }

    public function render()
    {
        $cars = DataFrame::fromRows(Datasets::mpg());

        return view('livewire.fuel-dashboard', fuel_dashboard(
            $cars,
            $this->drive,
            $this->year,
            $this->selected,
        ));
    }
}
```

- **Shareable state.** `#[Url]` keeps the drive and year in the query string, so a filtered view can be bookmarked.
- **Data source.** The example reads the bundled `mpg` data. An application would use `DataFrame::fromQuery()` or a cached table.
- **Toggle.** Selecting the selected class again clears the selection.

### The view

`resources/views/livewire/fuel-dashboard.blade.php`:

```blade
<div class="space-y-4">
    <div class="flex gap-4">
        <select wire:model.live="drive">
            <option value="">All drives</option>
            <option value="f">Front</option>
            <option value="r">Rear</option>
            <option value="4">4WD</option>
        </select>
        <select wire:model.live="year">
            <option value="">Both years</option>
            <option value="1999">1999</option>
            <option value="2008">2008</option>
        </select>
    </div>

    <div class="grid grid-cols-3 gap-4">
        <x-phiz :plot="$bars" wire:key="bars" />
        <x-phiz :plot="$scatter" wire:key="scatter" />
        <x-phiz :plot="$trend" wire:key="trend" />
    </div>

    <ul class="flex gap-2 text-sm">
        @foreach ($summary->toRows() as $row)
            <li><button wire:click="select('{{ $row['class'] }}')">
                {{ $row['class'] }} ({{ $row['cars'] }})
            </button></li>
        @endforeach
    </ul>
</div>
```

- **`wire:key`.** Each chart keeps its element across renders, and only charts whose specification changed are redrawn.
- **Grid cells.** The charts have container width, so each fills its grid cell.

### Clicks on a chart

The loader dispatches a `phiz:rendered` event with the Vega view. An Alpine handler can forward a click on a bar to the component:

```blade
<div x-on:phiz:rendered="
    $event.detail.view.addEventListener('click', (e, item) =>
        item?.datum?.class && $wire.select(item.datum.class))
">
    <x-phiz :plot="$bars" wire:key="bars" />
</div>
```

## Linking in the browser

When the data is small enough to send to the page, a composition can link charts with no server request. Brushing the scatterplot filters the bar chart, and Vega-Lite recomputes the means in the browser.

{{< include _generated/dashboard-client.md >}}

## Server or browser computation {#choosing-where-to-compute}

- **Server-side summaries** send only summarized rows. They suit large tables, database queries, and statistics computed in PHP, such as model fits. Each interaction is a Livewire request.
- **Browser-side linking** sends the raw rows once and responds without a request. It suits up to a few thousand rows ([Large data](large-data.qmd)).
- **Both** can share a page: a Livewire filter chooses the rows, and a brush explores them in the browser.

## A complete dashboard

[A complete dashboard](https://phiz.phpstats.org/vignettes/rent-dashboard) on phpstats.org adds a logistic model fitted with phit and what-if predictions to a Livewire page with filters, a phplyr summary, and two phiz charts.
